findings.title: Existing paginator now passes negative offsets to the queryset for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` leaves the offset unclamped for prev cursors. A client-supplied cursor with `is_prev=1` and a negative offset, for example `x:-1:1`, makes `queryset[-1:...]` raise an AssertionError. Before this change the same input also failed, but the change adds a comment claiming it is intended. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the raw offset, which no longer matches the `stop` value. Clamp the offset for all cursors, or validate it in `Cursor`.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on a Django queryset raises an error, and the cursor is user-controlled
findings.body: With `enable_advanced_features` set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets reject negative indexing with `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. Any admin can send `optimized_pagination=true` with a cursor like `0:-5:1` and get a 500. If the slice were allowed, it would read rows outside the pagination bounds. Reject or clamp negative offsets, and don't add this path.

findings.title: Privilege check may crash when member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the organization. A non-superuser request would then hit `.has_global_access` on None and raise AttributeError. The expression is also evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested, so this can break the default path. Compute it only when `use_optimized` is true, and guard against a None member.

findings.title: Duplicated paginator code has an inconsistent boundary check
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies `BasePaginator.get_result` and drops its explanatory comments. For the `is_prev` case it compares `len(results)` against `offset + limit + extra` using the raw offset, not `start_offset`. With a negative offset this never matches, so the extra row is not trimmed and pages come back one item too long. Reuse the base implementation, or use `start_offset` here.
